movements: marching in place, push-up, lateral lunge, glute bridge, prone y t w raise, forearm plank, figure-four stretch, belly breathing

@@ 55 | Welcome and the rules
Hi Jo, Coach Freya here, and welcome to our first session together. Fifteen minutes, bodyweight only, and quiet for the hotel room.

Your left knee stays light today, only as deep as it's comfortable and no jumping, and a pinch at the front or a catch means stop that move.

A little discomfort, two or three out of ten, is fine. Sharp pain or new swelling means stop that movement. Numbness, tingling, dizziness or a joint giving way means we're done for today.

Chest pain or pressure, feeling faint, or a racing or pounding heart means stop the whole session and get help.

And plainly, an AI put this session together, not a certified trainer or a clinician, so your body and your doctor have the final say.

@@ 80 | Warm-up, marching in place, sixty seconds easy
Stand tall for marching in place, feet under your hips, arms loose. First, grab a towel, fold it and set it on the floor. Any time we kneel, it goes under your left knee.

March brisk, like a walk you could chat through, opposite arm swinging, feet landing soft and quiet. The left knee lifts only as high as is easy. [count 3 go]

Easy rhythm, quiet feet.

Jo, you loved The Right Stuff and Apollo Thirteen, so here's a near miss from that era, with Neil Armstrong before the Moon.

[story]March sixteenth, nineteen sixty-six, Gemini Eight. Armstrong in command, David Scott beside him.

The job was the first docking in space ever, with an uncrewed target called the Agena, a trick Apollo would depend on. And they nailed it, clean.

Then about twenty-seven minutes later, while the Agena turned them ninety degrees as planned, Scott noticed they were rolling too.

Armstrong fired the thrusters and it stopped, then started again and got worse, a roll and a tumble together. They were out of touch with Houston, far from any tracking station.

Sure the Agena was at fault and might break apart, they decided to undock. That made things much worse.[/story]

That's halfway, keep it brisk and quiet.

Last ten seconds, stand tall, shoulders easy.

And done. Down to the floor, ready for push-ups.

@@ 45 | Push-up set 1, 10 reps, bodyweight
Push-ups, Jo. Hands under your shoulders, one long line from head to heels, or knees down on the towel. Chest toward the floor, then press to straight arms. Ten, two left in the tank. [count 3 go] [reps 10]

Smooth down, press up. [hold 3s] Hips sagging? Squeeze and brace. [hold 3s] Halfway, keep the line. [hold 3s] Last two, clean ones. [hold 3s] And rest.

Too easy? Three seconds down next round. Too hard? Hands on the bed edge. Now stand up.

@@ 40 | Lateral lunge set 1, right side only, 10 reps, bodyweight
Up you come. Lateral lunges on the right side only today, the left leg resting, and training the good side still helps the sore one a little.

Feet together, hands at your chest. Step wide to the right, toes forward, sit into the right hip, then push back to the middle. Ten, two in the tank. [count 3 go] [reps 10]

Step, sit, push back. [hold 3s] Right knee over the middle of your foot. [hold 3s] Halfway, nice and smooth. [hold 3s] Last two. [hold 2s] Good, and rest.

Easy? Slower sit. Inner thigh pulling? Shorter step.

@@ 50 | Glute bridge set 1, 15 reps, bodyweight, light
Onto your back, knees bent, feet flat. Glute bridges: for a sore knee, working the hips along with the knee does more than knee work alone. Hips up, squeeze, lower slow. Fifteen, light. [count 3 go] [reps 15]

Lift, squeeze, lower. [hold 3s] Ribs stay down. [hold 3s] Halfway, steady. [hold 3s] Keep it smooth. [hold 3s] Last three. [hold 3s] And rest. Roll face down.

@@ 40 | Prone y t w raise set 1, 10 reps, bodyweight
Face down, forehead on the towel or your hands. Prone Y T W raises: arms up in a Y, out in a T, elbows in for a W, thumbs up, shoulders down.

All three is one rep, between the shoulder blades, not the neck. Ten, two in the tank. [count 3 go] [reps 10]

Y, T, W, slow. [hold 3s] Neck straining? Forehead stays down. [hold 3s] Halfway, nice and slow. [hold 3s] Last two. [hold 3s] And rest.

Easy? Pause on each letter next round. Tough? Smaller lifts.

@@ 65 | Rest
Stay right where you are and let one long breath out. That's round one, Jo, four moves in the bank.

Here's something to chew on, since Kind of Blue got a five from you.

[story]Myth or fact: the whole of Kind of Blue was recorded in one pass, every tune a first take, nothing done again. Some setup.

It's Miles Davis and his sextet, at Columbia's Thirtieth Street Studio in New York City, and the band famously got very little to work from ahead of time.

So, does that add up to one clean pass, straight through? Or did somebody, somewhere, go again? Think it over through the next round, and I'll give you the answer after it.[/story]

Round two starts with push-ups. Get set on your hands, or knees on the towel, with whatever change you picked.

@@ 35 | Push-up set 2, 10 reps, bodyweight
Round two, ten push-ups. Take the change you picked, the slower lowering or hands on the bed edge. Push the floor away, one long line, two in the tank. [count 3 go] [reps 10]
Push the floor away. [hold 3s] Long line. [hold 3s] Chest low, then press. [hold 3s] Halfway there. [hold 3s] Last two. [hold 4s] And rest.

@@ 30 | Lateral lunge set 2, right side only, 10 reps, bodyweight
Up to standing, no rush. Right-side lateral lunges, ten on the right, with your change. Sit back into the hip, whole foot down. [count 3 go] [reps 10]
Sit back, whole foot down. [hold 3s] Push back to the middle. [hold 3s] Halfway, smooth. [hold 3s] Stay tall through the chest. [hold 3s] Last two. [hold 3s] And rest.

@@ 45 | Glute bridge set 2, 15 reps, bodyweight, light
Down onto your back. Glute bridges, fifteen, light, three or more left, steady or the smaller lift, whichever you chose. Squeeze and hold one beat at the top. [count 3 go] [reps 15]
Lift, and hold a beat. [hold 4s] Lower slow. [hold 4s] Ribs stay down. [hold 3s] Halfway, steady. [hold 4s] Squeeze at the top. [hold 4s] Backs of the hips doing the work. [hold 3s] Last three. [hold 4s] And rest.

@@ 35 | Prone y t w raise set 2, 10 reps, bodyweight
Roll face down. Prone Y T W raises, ten, with the pause at each letter if you chose it. Shoulders away from your ears. [count 3 go] [reps 10]
Y, T, W. [hold 3s] Shoulders down, away from the ears. [hold 3s] Halfway now. [hold 3s] Last two. [hold 3s] And rest. Straight onto your forearms for the plank.

@@ 50 | Forearm plank, forty seconds, bodyweight
Forearm plank, a new one. Elbows under your shoulders, legs long, or knees on the towel. Glutes tight, ribs down, one long line.

Belly and glutes working, no pinch in the low back. Forty seconds, a little left at the end. [count 3 go]

Settle the breath, slow and even.

Back to Gemini Eight, Jo.

[story]Scott hit undock, and without the heavier Agena they spun faster, up to one full turn every second. He told a stunned Mission Control they were tumbling end over end.[/story]

Halfway, hold that line.

[story]They were close to blacking out. The real culprit was thruster number eight on their own craft, stuck open. Armstrong shut that system off, switched to the nose thrusters, and the spin stopped.

Forty months later, he commanded Apollo Eleven. Cool head, right seat.[/story]

Last ten seconds. If the hips sag, glutes tight and ribs down. [hold]

And rest, knees down.

@@ 65 | Rest
Rest, and one long breath out. Plank done, two rounds in the bank.

Now, that question about Kind of Blue.

[story]One pass, every tune a first take? Myth. It took two sessions at Columbia's Thirtieth Street Studio, March second and April twenty-second, nineteen fifty-nine.

So What, Freddie Freeloader and Blue in Green came first. All Blues and Flamenco Sketches came second.

And there are false starts and alternate takes. The session log lists a false start on Freddie Freeloader and an alternate take of Flamenco Sketches.

The legend comes from how little rehearsal there was. Davis handed the band only sketches of scales and melody lines, and in his autobiography he said he wanted a lot of spontaneity in the playing.

No rehearsal, but not no retakes.[/story]

Loose, but they went again when it mattered, and so do we. Last round, push-ups first. Hands set.

@@ 35 | Push-up set 3, 10 reps, bodyweight
Last round, Jo. Ten push-ups with your change, and this one goes to one left in the tank. Elbows at a gentle angle. [count 3 go] [reps 10]
Strong and smooth. [hold 3s] Elbows at that gentle angle. [hold 3s] Halfway, keep pushing. [hold 3s] Dig in, last two. [hold 3s] That's it, and rest.

@@ 30 | Lateral lunge set 3, right side only, 10 reps, bodyweight
Up to standing, take your time. Last set of right-side lateral lunges, ten on the right, two in the tank. Keep that right knee pointing over your mid-foot. [count 3 go] [reps 10]
Sit back, push home. [hold 3s] Knee in line with the foot. [hold 3s] Halfway there. [hold 3s] Last two. [hold 3s] And rest.

@@ 45 | Glute bridge set 3, 15 reps, bodyweight, light
Down onto your back. Last fifteen glute bridges, still light, three or more left. Ribs down, and lower one notch at a time. [count 3 go] [reps 15]
Lift and squeeze. [hold 4s] Lower notch by notch. [hold 4s] Ribs stay down. [hold 4s] Halfway, steady. [hold 4s] Smooth on the way down. [hold 3s] Squeeze at the top. [hold 3s] Last three. [hold 4s] And rest.

@@ 35 | Prone y t w raise set 3, 10 reps, bodyweight
Roll face down. Last ten prone Y T W raises, small and slow, two in the tank. Thumbs up the whole way. [count 3 go] [reps 10]
Thumbs up. [hold 3s] Small and slow. [hold 3s] Shoulders away from the ears. [hold 3s] Halfway now. [hold 3s] Last two. [hold 4s] And rest.

That's three rounds in the bank. Roll onto your back.

@@ 50 | Cool-down, figure-four stretch, thirty seconds a side
On your back, knees bent. Figure-four stretch. Cross your right ankle over your left knee, reach behind the bottom thigh, and draw it gently in, crossed foot flexed. Head and shoulders stay down.

You're after a mild stretch deep in the glute, no pinch in the knee. If the knee complains, keep the foot flexed and ease the pull. Breathe slow, and let the hip open a little on each breath out.

Good. Now switch. Uncross, and take a few seconds to set the left ankle over the right knee.

Same again, hold behind the bottom thigh and draw it in gently, foot flexed. If the knee complains, keep the foot flexed and ease off. Let the breath do the work, head down, shoulders soft.

@@ 70 | Cool-down, belly breathing, sixty seconds
Come up to sit tall, on the floor or the bed edge. One hand on your chest, one on your belly. Slow breaths now, the belly rises and the chest hand stays still.

Long breaths out settle your heart rate and bring you down. We'll do five, in for four, out for six. If you feel dizzy, just breathe normally.

Breathe in, belly rises.

And out, long and slow.

Two, in through the nose.

Out, all the way.

Three, in, chest stays still.

Out, slower still.

Four, breathe in.

And let it go.

Last one, in.

Out, long and easy.

That's it, Jo. Three rounds of push-ups, right-side lateral lunges, glute bridges and prone Y T W raises, plus a forearm plank, all on a hotel floor.

Next time we'll see how that knee is doing and build from today. How hard did that feel, out of ten?

stories.title: Gemini VIII, part one: the first docking
stories.text:
Why it's Jo's: a near miss from the era of The Right Stuff and Apollo Thirteen, both in their Taste, with Neil Armstrong before the Moon.
March 16, 1966: Gemini VIII, command pilot Neil Armstrong, pilot David Scott.
The job: the world's first docking in space, with an uncrewed Agena target vehicle. Apollo would depend on that technique.
They made it. First docking ever, a clean one (AmericaSpace calls it flawless).
Then, about 27 minutes later, while the Agena turned the joined craft 90 degrees as planned, Scott noticed they were also rolling.
Armstrong used Gemini's thrusters to stop it. It stopped, then started again and got worse: a roll and a tumble together.
They were out of touch with Houston, far from any tracking station.
They feared the Agena might break apart and blow up, and believed it was the one at fault.
Hook: so they decided to undock. That made things much worse. Continue in piece 3.

stories.topic: Space history: the missions, the people, the near misses
stories.title: Gemini VIII, part two: the spin
stories.text:
Where we were: Armstrong and Scott, docked and tumbling, blaming the Agena, about to undock.
Scott hit the undock button. Without the heavier Agena, the Gemini tumbled much faster, reaching a roll rate of one rotation per second (NASA).
Scott to a stunned Mission Control: "We have serious problems here. We're tumbling end over end."
They were close to blacking out and struggled to read their instruments.
The real cause, found later: thruster number 8 on their own Gemini had short-circuited and stuck open.
Armstrong shut down the main thruster system and switched on the reentry control system thrusters in the nose. The spin stopped, but it used three-quarters of that propellant (Smithsonian).
Mission rules then required landing at the next chance. Scott's spacewalk was cancelled.
Scott later: "The guy was brilliant. He knew the system so well."
Lands on: forty months later, Armstrong commanded Apollo 11 (Smithsonian). Keeping a cool head in a spin is part of why he got that seat.

stories.title: Kind of Blue in one take? (answered)
stories.text:
Pays off piece 1: was Kind of Blue recorded in one pass?
Answer: myth. Wikipedia: "the persistent legend that the entire album was recorded in one pass is untrue."
The reason: two sessions at Columbia's 30th Street Studio, March 2 and April 22, 1959. Side one (So What, Freddie Freeloader, Blue in Green) came first; All Blues and Flamenco Sketches came second.
There are false starts and alternate takes: Mosaic's session log lists a false start on Freddie Freeloader and an alternate take of Flamenco Sketches.
Where the legend comes from: almost no rehearsal. Davis gave the band only sketches of scales and melody lines.
Davis, in his 1989 autobiography: "I wanted a lot of spontaneity in the playing."
Lands on: no rehearsal is not the same as no retakes. They were loose, but they still went again when it mattered, much like the next set.

stories.title: The wheel at Johnsville
stories.text:
Why it's Jo's: the Mercury Seven from The Right Stuff, and links to the Gemini spin.
The Johnsville human centrifuge, run by the Navy in Warminster, Pennsylvania, was nicknamed the wheel. It trained the Mercury, Gemini and Apollo astronauts.
John Glenn called it "dreaded" and "sadistic". Michael Collins called it "diabolical."
The training detail: astronauts learned to fight G forces with breathing techniques and muscle contractions.
Glenn: "You were straining every muscle of your body to the maximum"; ease up and your vision narrowed and you started to black out.
Scott Carpenter worked out a breathing technique "akin to explosive grunting" to handle high Gs (Pennsylvania Center for the Book).
Link to this set: the same pairing of breath and brace that keeps a strength rep steady. The idea is tension and breath working together, not holding on blindly.

stories.text:
Why it's Jo's: they loved Kind of Blue (a five), and its pianist was Bill Evans. This is where Evans went next with his own trio.
What it is: Sunday at the Village Vanguard, a live album by the Bill Evans Trio: Evans, bassist Scott LaFaro, drummer Paul Motian.
The concrete detail: recorded June 25, 1961 at the Village Vanguard in New York City, over five sets in one day, two in the afternoon and three in the evening.
LaFaro died in a car accident about ten days later. The tracks were picked to feature his bass, opening and closing with two of his own tunes, Gloria's Step and Jade Visions.
Evans: "I am thankful that we recorded that day, because it was the last time I saw Scott"
Its companion from the same day is Waltz for Debby.
Lands on: a calm one for a hotel room after training, three players listening to each other as equals.
